extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency officials (agency heads), agency HR/personnel offices, and OPM staff responsible for reemployment of annuitants; legal counsel advising agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory criteria and procedural requirements (5 CFR Part 553) governing when and how agencies may request OPM approval or delegation to reemploy civilian retirees/annuitants without reduction or termination of annuity to meet exceptional hiring, recruiting, or retention needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This part applies to employment of civilian annuitants who would be subject to termination of annuity or annuity offset under 5 U.S.C. 8344 or 5 U.S.C. 8468. Agencies may request exceptions as provided in subpart B of this part from the reemployed annuitant provisions of 5 U.S.C. 8344 or 8468, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Agency, Annuitant, Retiree)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency means an executive agency as defined in 5 U.S.C. 105. Annuitant refers to a current or former civilian employee who is receiving, or meets the legal requirements and is applying or has announced intention to apply for, an annuity under subchapter III of chapter 83 or chapter 84 of title 5 based on service. Retiree refers to an annuitant as defined above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency discretion and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to request an exception, or to grant an exception under delegated authority, for any individual under any of the provisions of this part will be at the discretion of the employing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination made for one position does not require a like determination for another. In deciding whether to request or grant an exception, agencies are expected to weigh fiscal responsibility and employee equity and should consider factors such as availability of funds as well as the criteria set out in this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of exceptions (scope and duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: An exception authorized by OPM or an agency under this part applies only to the particular individual for whom it was authorized and only while that individual continues to serve in the same or a successor position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception terminates upon the individual's assignment to a different position unless a new exception is authorized under the provisions of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request OPM approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of an agency may request OPM to approve individual exceptions on a case-by-case basis to meet temporary hiring needs based on an emergency or other unusual circumstances or when the agency has encountered exceptional difficulty in recruiting or retaining a qualified candidate for a particular position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to submit such a request may not be redelegated to an official below the agency's headquarters level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for all requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request must identify the individual for whom the exception is requested, the appointing authority to be used, and the position to which he or she will be appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be submitted in accordance with the criteria set out in paragraphs (c), (d), (e), or (f) of §553.201. Unless the request is submitted under paragraph (e) (retention), the individual must be off the agency's rolls before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests based on an emergency hiring need (nature of emergency)
rubrics_metrics.description: For emergencies involving a direct threat to life or property, the request must describe the military threat, natural disaster, or other unforeseen occurrence, the date it occurred, and the expected duration of the emergency response effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must show either that the individual is uniquely qualified for the emergency response work or that the number of positions and/or urgency justifies making the appointment without further delay. OPM will not approve reemployment without penalty solely to meet normal seasonal workload fluctuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests based on severe recruiting difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests based on exceptional difficulty in recruiting a qualified candidate must include a description of the length, breadth, and results of the agency's recruiting efforts for the position and any other factors demonstrating that a legitimate recruiting need cannot be met without the requested waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors may include, but are not limited to, unusual qualification requirements or working conditions, possibility of job reengineering or contracting, or a need to fill the position without further delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions based on need to retain a particular individual — critical nature of project
rubrics_metrics.description: In very rare cases, an exception may be appropriate when an agency needs to retain the services of a particular individual who is uniquely qualified for an ongoing project. The agency must describe the importance of the project to the agency's mission, the potential costs of project failure or delay, legislative or Presidential deadlines, if any, and other factors demonstrating the project is unusually critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions will not be approved merely to avoid delay in scheduled completion of ongoing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions based on need to retain a particular individual — candidate's unique qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must describe the knowledges, skills, and abilities possessed by the individual that are essential for successful completion of the project and that could not be acquired by another appointee within a reasonable time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions based on need to retain a particular individual — need for retention
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must show good cause to believe that the employee will retire (or, if currently reemployed without an exception, will resign from that position) and that the agency will lose his or her services if the exception is not granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions based on need to retain a particular individual — other staffing options
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must address why the work could not be assigned to other employees involved with the same project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not required to conduct outside recruiting in these rare retention cases, the agency must explain why other staffing options are not feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests based on other unusual circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may request reemployment without penalty for an individual whose services are needed on a temporary basis due to other unusual circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide a justification describing the unusual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of exceptions and renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM may specify a time limit for reemployment without penalty of any individual approved under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agency wishes to continue the exception beyond the specified time, the renewal request must demonstrate that the conditions justifying the initial exception still exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for delegation of authority — who may request
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of an agency may request OPM to delegate to the agency authority to approve individual exceptions on a case-by-case basis in specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to submit such a request may not be redelegated to an official below the agency's headquarters level (or, for DoD, below the military department or Defense agency headquarters level).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of delegation request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for delegation must include: (1) description of the situations for which authority is requested (emergencies posing immediate and direct threat to life or property or other unusual circumstances), (2) identification of the occupations, grades, and locations of positions that might be filled under the delegated authority, and (3) statement of the expected duration of the reemployment to be approved under the requested authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation agreement conditions and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM will set out the conditions for use of each delegated authority in a delegation agreement. The agreement will remain in effect without time limit unless OPM specifies a termination date or withdraws the delegated authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM may withdraw delegation upon finding that circumstances justifying the delegation have changed substantially or that the agency has failed to manage the authority in accordance with the law, regulations, and the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status and limitations of individuals serving without reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Annuitants reemployed with full salary and annuity under an exception granted in accordance with this part are not considered employees for purposes of subchapter III of chapter 83 or chapter 84 of title 5, United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may not elect to have retirement contributions withheld from their pay; may not use such employment as a basis for a supplemental or recomputed annuity; and may not participate in the Thrift Savings Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority for these provisions: 5 U.S.C. 8344, 8468, Sec. 651, Pub. L. 106-65 (113 STAT. 664).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source: 56 FR 6206, Feb. 14, 1991, as amended. (Citation provided to indicate statutory/legal basis for the rules.)
